data.title: PTC Expands FedRAMP Offerings to Help U.S. Federal Agencies and Contractors Modernize Product Development
data.description:
• Adds Windchill+ as the only direct, full-stack SaaS PLM solution certified on the FedRAMP Marketplace
  • Introduces Onshape Government Federal as the only cloud-native CAD and PDM solution for engineering teams working with CUI
  • Expands PTC's FedRAMP portfolio as part of its long-term commitment to the federal market

BOSTON, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PTC () today announced an expansion of its FedRAMP offerings for U.S. federal agencies and contractors. PTC's Windchill+® product lifecycle management (PLM) solution is now available on Microsoft Azure Government within PTC Cloud Services, and PTC is introducing its Onshape® Government Federal solution, a FedRAMP Moderate Equivalent environment for engineering teams working with Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). The two new offerings also support compliance with the Department of Defense's Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) program for protecting CUI.

Windchill+ is the only direct, full-stack SaaS PLM solution certified on the FedRAMP Marketplace. PTC Cloud Services is certified at the FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) baseline (NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5), so agencies can rely on an existing certification rather than running their own security review.

Onshape Government Federal is the only cloud-native CAD and PDM with a FedRAMP Moderate Equivalent attestation based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5. Built on AWS GovCloud (US), it expands its existing support for ITAR and EAR workloads. It also integrates with the Arena® PLM for AWS GovCloud solution, giving organizations a connected CAD, PDM, and PLM environment across engineering, quality, and supply chain workflows.

"Aerospace and defense organizations build and maintain some of the most complex, mission-critical products in the world," said Jon Stevenson, Chief Product Officer, PTC. "For nearly a decade, we've invested in cloud solutions that meet federal security requirements, and we aim to continue that investment so these customers can count on PTC from product design through service."

PTC Cloud Services first achieved FedRAMP authorization in 2017, and PTC has expanded its federal portfolio steadily ever since. In addition to Windchill+ and Onshape, federal agencies and contractors can choose from these PTC solutions to manage product data while meeting federal security requirements:

  • Windchill SaaS: DoD Impact Level 4 and 5 (IL4 and IL5) authorized
  • Arena: Cloud-native PLM and quality management system (QMS), FedRAMP Moderate Equivalent
  • Servigistics: Service parts planning and optimization, IL5 authorized

Across its portfolio, PTC is delivering on its vision for the Intelligent Product Lifecycle: enabling manufacturers to build a modern product data foundation, extend that data across the enterprise, and unlock AI-powered transformation. Broader use of product data enables companies to bring higher-quality products to market faster, manage complexity at scale, and support new digital business models.

About PTC

PTC () is a global software company that enables manufacturers and product companies to digitally transform how they design, manufacture, and service the physical products that the world relies on. Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, PTC employs over 7,000 people and supports more than 30,000 customers globally.

data.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Convene First-Ever Summit as World Order Shifts — WSJ
data.description:
By Vera Bergengruen, Jonathan Cheng and Marianne LeVine

SHENZHEN, China — President Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, stewards of the world's three largest nuclear arsenals, joined together in this southern Chinese city for an unprecedented show of unity on Thursday.

The first-ever gathering of the American, Chinese and Russian leaders was a further sign of the end of a unipolar world order dominated by the U.S. — and suggested that what might replace it is a more uncertain, and unsettled, reality.

"We are really making history," Trump said as they opened the 90-minute meeting, sitting around a large, round wooden table under a towering Chinese landscape painting. "No problems were ever solved under the old school, refusing to talk about them."

In the end, the meeting yielded at least an indication of consensus on several topics on the U.S. president's agenda, according to joint statements issued by Russia and China. The U.S. has yet to issue its version of the agreements.

The leaders said their countries would engage in a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing nuclear proliferation, and plan to increase global supply of refined petroleum products, among other points of agreement, according to the Russian and Chinese statements.

Despite indications of common ground, the three men remain divided by their competing ambitions and sharply conflicting visions of what a new world order should look like.

Russia and the U.S. are bogged down in wars, while Beijing faces mounting economic problems and is deeply reluctant to take on the kind of global leadership role historically played by the U.S.

What the three leaders do share is a desire to be able to operate without constraints in their respective spheres.

Putin wants Washington to stay out of his way in Ukraine. Xi wants the U.S. to accept his claim that self-ruled Taiwan belongs to China. And Trump has made pushing Chinese and Russian influence out of the Western Hemisphere a central element of his so-called "Donroe Doctrine" to reassert U.S. dominance in the region.

There was little indication that progress could be made on the major issues they brought to the table: the wars in Ukraine and Iran and the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

But for the men in the spotlight, just sitting down together was the point.

They met at Kylin Villa, a secluded government guesthouse at the foot of the hills of Shenzhen that has hosted China's political elite and foreign dignitaries.

Going into the meeting, Trump embraced the historic gathering to promote an image of himself as a global peacemaker alongside two autocrats whom he has long admired.

"All my life I read you'd never want to have Russia and China team up. That was like 101 in politics or in warfare," Trump said in a Fox News interview before the meeting. "They both like Trump. Now, what happens after me? That I can't tell you."

He left Washington with his party reeling from its midterm defeats, eager to use his final two years in office to cement his legacy on the world stage. "We have a chance to accomplish a lot," he said as he departed for Asia.

Trump headed first to a meeting of Southeast Asian leaders in Manila and then to Shenzhen for the annual APEC gathering of Asia-Pacific leaders, hosted this year by China.

When Trump landed Wednesday in Shenzhen, Xi welcomed him with the pomp Trump relishes, personally greeting him on the tarmac, a first by a Chinese president, and arranging a colorful military flyover — just as Trump did for Xi on his arrival in the U.S. in September.

Trump offered little indication of what he hoped to accomplish with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen, beyond opening talks on nuclear arms control. U.S. officials played down any prospects of a breakthrough.

Trump acknowledged in the Fox News interview that reaching an agreement on reducing nuclear arsenals would be challenging.

"When they look at me and they say, 'OK we'll do it, but will you reduce your nuclear weapons by 2,000 weapons?'...It's a hard thing to do," Trump said. "For me, it's a hard thing. And it's probably hard for them to do also."

The New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty, or New START, the last treaty limiting Washington and Moscow's strategic nuclear arsenals, expired earlier this year. Trump has pushed for a broader agreement that would include China, whose rapid rise as a nuclear power brings new complications to any denuclearization effort.

Trump had also repeatedly floated the prospect that his trip to Asia would include a meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, who is building his own nuclear arsenal. He left Shenzhen without confirming whether such a meeting would take place.

For Putin, the gathering marked a remarkable diplomatic comeback nearly five years after his invasion of Ukraine made him an international pariah.

"He's my friend," Trump said after greeting the Russian leader for a two-way meeting earlier in the day. "We knew each other for a long time, and I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this."

Trump later said he and Putin had a lengthy discussion on Ukraine, suggesting there had been progress without offering specifics. "I think things are happening," he said.

The Russian leader had first proposed a trilateral summit alongside the APEC meetings as a venue to discuss ending the Ukraine war.

In the end, Putin's place at the sit-down with the leaders of the world's two largest economies underscored the limits of Western efforts to isolate him.

"Our three nations are united not only by the status of victors in the Second World War but mainly by our responsibility for maintaining international peace," Putin said at the meeting.

Xi, while playing host, has in some ways been the reluctant party among the three. Beijing has long said that it doesn't belong in arms-control talks, saying its arsenal is dwarfed by those of Washington and Moscow.

But Xi benefits just by being there. The meeting places the Chinese leader on an equal footing, for the third time this year, with the U.S. president, while standing alongside a close partner in Putin over whom he holds an overwhelming advantage.

"What Xi gains from this trilateral meeting is the chance to look like the pivot player in international politics, convening this would-be 'G3' on Chinese soil and sitting alongside his closest partner on the world stage, Putin, to negotiate with a remarkably friendly American president," said Julian Gewirtz, a China-focused official in the Biden-era National Security Council.

As Trump met with Xi ahead of the trilateral, he framed his "very special relationship" with the Chinese leader as the cornerstone of U.S.-China stability.

"As long as you and I are in charge of things, we'll never have a problem," Trump said as he met with Xi. "We're never gonna have a problem."

Write to Vera Bergengruen at vera.bergengruen@wsj.com, Jonathan Cheng at Jonathan.Cheng@wsj.com and Marianne LeVine at marianne.levine@wsj.com

data.title: Poland Closes in on Construction Deal With U.S. Consortium for $50 Billion Nuclear Power Plant — Update
data.description:
By Adam Whittaker

WARSAW--Poland expects to sign a deal with an American consortium to build the country's first nuclear power plant early next year, as the European nation pushes to bolster its energy security after war disrupted the region's supplies.

Polskie Elektrownie Jadrowe is in the final stages of negotiations with U.S. nuclear technology company Westinghouse Electric and construction giant Bechtel Group Inc. to ink an engineering, procurement and construction contract for Poland's roughly $50 billion new nuclear plant, the head of the state-owned entity told Dow Jones Newswires.

Signing by the end of the first quarter of next year looks most likely, the president of PEJ's management board, Marek Woszczyk, said in an interview on the sidelines of the Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation conference in Poland. The three parties had said they hoped to sign the contract by the end of the year.

A delayed signing won't hold up the project's timeline, Woszczyk said. The first reactor is due online in 2036, with reactors two and three coming online in 2037 and 2038, respectively, he said.

The project consists of three Westinghouse AP1000 reactors, with a total capacity of 3,750 megawatts electric. The Westinghouse-Bechtel consortium will be responsible for the construction of the facility. Electricity from the power plant is expected to be supplied to the Polish grid starting from 2036, according to PEJ.

Bolstering Poland's energy security and minimizing dependency on others is at the heart of the country's nuclear program, Woszczyk said. PEJ will buy nuclear fuel from several different suppliers to ensure it's never reliant on just one source and plans to store nuclear fuel on site to minimize the potential for supply disruptions, Woszczyk added.

Poland wants to be as independent as possible when it comes to energy, he said.

Historically reliant on neighbor Russia for its energy supplies, Poland shunned its dependency after the invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and is forging ahead with an energy mix underpinned by LNG and nuclear technology from the U.S.

There is no going back to business with Russia, Polish Energy Minister Milosz Motyka said at the conference this week.

"Russia used energy sources like a weapon," he added.

Located on the banks of the Baltic Sea in Pomerania, the reactors will provide around 10% of the country's electricity based on current forecasts, Woszczyk said. The broader energy mix will be supplemented by renewable energy and natural gas as coal power plants are phased out.

It's no surprise that American technology and providers were selected to build the reactors. The AP1000 reactor is proven technology and Poland wants to reinforce its ties to the U.S., Woszczyk said.

The Trump administration has made energy dominance a key part of its foreign policy. It has pushed allies in Europe to buy U.S.-extracted hydrocarbons, and Poland has been one of the most prolific signers of long-term deals.

Discussions with Poland on nuclear energy cooperation started during President Trump's first term and the push continued under the Biden administration. The U.S. Energy Department considers Poland's decision to buy U.S. nuclear technology as a model that can be replicated in neighboring countries.

Poland's nuclear project puts Westinghouse and the U.S. firmly at the forefront of Europe's nuclear renaissance, Caspar Hobhouse, research analyst at the European Union Institute for Security Studies, said.

PEJ has plans for more nuclear power plants and is in talks with French, Canadian and U.S. providers on another power plant elsewhere in the country, Woszczyk said.

Write to Adam Whittaker at Adam.Whittaker@wsj.com

data.title: The Rationale Behind Palo Alto's AI-Startup Acquisition — Market Talk
data.description: Palo Alto Networks' $4.5 billion acquisition of Applied Compute initially appeared to pull the company outside of its traditional cybersecurity lane, but the call clarified the strategic logic, StoneX says in a research note. In short: Palo Alto believes it must help build AI before it can credibly secure AI. "Effective AI supervision ultimately requires independently trained models that understand how an application was built, how it should behave, and when it deviates," analyst Yi Fu Lee says. "Applied Compute brings the post-training platform and scarce research talent needed to develop that supervision layer, train Palo Alto Networks' proprietary large and small models, and help enterprises deploy secure open-weight AI in public and sovereign-cloud environments." Palo Alto shares are up 6.5%. (connor.hart@wsj.com)

data.title: Robusta coffee falls to 2-1/2-year low, cocoa climbs
data.description:
Robusta coffee futures on ICE fell to a 2-1/2-year low on Thursday with supplies boosted by newly harvested beans from Vietnam while cocoa prices rose.

COFFEE

* Robusta coffee fell 1.95% to $2,960 a metric ton by 1433 GMT after setting a 2-1/2-year low of $2,945

* Dealers said the flow of newly harvested robusta beans from Vietnam had contributed to the recent decline in prices while the recent weakness of Brazil's real had encouraged exports from the world's top coffee producer.

* "Expectations of increased global supplies are weighing on prices with the Vietnam harvest underway and the weak Brazilian real encouraging exports," said a trader based in Vietnam

* Arabica coffee rose 0.5% to $2.7680 per lb

COCOA

* London cocoa rose 4.2% to £4,055 a ton

* Dealers said low port arrivals in top grower Ivory Coast had helped to underpin the market with the El Nino weather event set to curb global production in the 2026/27 season

* Ample availability of cocoa from the 2025/26 crop, however, continued to keep a lid on prices with exchange stocks well above year-ago levels.

* New York cocoa gained 4.4% to $5,223 a ton

SUGAR

* Raw sugar fell 2.2% to 17.65 cents per lb after setting a seven-week low of 17.62 cents.

* Dealers said funds have been scaling back a net long position in raw sugar with the market looking technically bearish after breaking below key support levels.

* Pakistan's state trading agency TCP is believed to have sold about 96,000 metric tons of white sugar in an international tender seeking to sell and export up to 108,000 tons, which closed last week, European traders said on Thursday

* White sugar lost 1.9% to $497.50 a ton

data.title: Quebecor Defends Telus Bid, Criticizes Potential BCE Countermove
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese

Quebecor pushed back against a potential rival tie-up between BCE and Telus, saying that a merger of the two major telecoms would hurt Canadian consumers.

The statement follows a Globe and Mail report on Wednesday that BCE's Bell Canada had opened preliminary talks with Telus to evaluate its options in response to Quebecor's unsolicited takeover bid.

Earlier in the week, Quebecor proposed a combination with Telus worth 31.31 billion Canadian dollars ($21.85 billion),or about C$19.45 a share, representing a roughly 60% premium to Telus' closing share price on the Toronto Stock Exchange last Friday, according to Quebecor.

Quebecor said Thursday that while Canada's telecommunication sector needs greater scale to compete with U.S. technology and satellite players, only its proposal would protect competition and lower prices.

BCE wasn't immediately available for comment.

The company added that it looks forward to meeting with Telus management on Nov. 23.

Write to Adriano Marchese at adriano.marchese@wsj.com

data.title: Alam Energy, Zeroboard to support corp decarbonisation in Indonesia
data.description:
November 19 (Renewables Now) - PT Alam Energy Renewables intends to support the decarbonisation management of companies in Indonesia as part of a new partnership with Zeroboard Inc, a Japanese cloud service for the calculation, disclosure and reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.

The two companies have signed an agreement to combine emissions visualisation with the offerings of Alam Energy, including rooftop solar power and renewable energy certificates (I-REC), it was announced on Wednesday.

The duo will hold joint seminars and provide support from emissions calculation to reduction for local companies, contributing to the domestic government’s goal to reach net zero emissions by 2060.

Alam Energy is owned by Shizen Energy Inc, Alamport Inc, NiX Japan Group, EnBio Holdings Inc and Kanematsu Corporation. As of October 2026, the business operates 39.5 MWp of rooftop solar power systems spread across 31 sites in Indonesia, mainly for Japanese manufacturers.

data.title: ASTS Stock Gets A Breather After Relentless Sell-Off: B. Riley Says Launch Delays, Funding Risks Are Already Priced In
data.description:
Key points:
  • B. Riley upgraded the satellite communications company to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral,’ according to The Fly.
  • On Wednesday, William Blair reiterated its ‘Market Perform’ rating on ASTS after ULA’s preliminary findings eased BE-4 engine concerns.
  • AST SpaceMobile is expected to use Blue Origin’s rockets with BE-4 engines next year.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) received an upgrade from B. Riley, which raised its rating to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral’ on Wednesday, stating that the shares have already priced in concerns over the company’s capital commitment, satellite deployment delays, and its rocket development partnership with Firefly Aerospace (FLY).

ASTS stock was up about 8% at the time of writing and on track for a first gain in six sessions. It has declined more than 39% over the past one month as of Wednesday’s close.

B. Riley Sees 73% Upside Potential

According to The Fly, B. Riley maintained its $48 price target on ASTS, implying a 73% upside from current levels. However, it is still well short of the 12-month consensus estimate of $63.35, according to Koyfin.

The firm now sees a more attractive risk-reward balance and believes investors are overlooking the potential benefits of developing its own launch capabilities, as well as “other positive catalysts.”

FireFly Partnership In Spotlight

B. Riley’s comments on AST SpaceMobile developing its own launch capabilities follow the company's announcement that it plans to develop its reusable Blacklift rocket, using Firefly’s Miranda and Vira engines, targeting launches starting in late 2028. On Tuesday, AST issued 10 million shares to Firefly under the agreement.

The partnership aims to reduce AST’s dependence on external launch providers and give it greater control over satellite deployments.

ULA’s Initial Findings Ease Engine Concerns

On Wednesday, William Blair reiterated its ‘Market Perform’ rating on ASTS after United Launch Alliance (ULA) said that preliminary findings from its November 15 Vulcan rocket launch failure, which destroyed 40 Amazon Leo satellites, pointed to inadequate fuel supply rather than performance of the BE-4 engines. The BE-4 rocket engine is developed by Blue Origin.

The findings are crucial because AST SpaceMobile expects to launch three BlueBird satellites aboard Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket in early 2027. New Glenn uses the same BE-4 engine model as Vulcan.

However, the investigation remains ongoing under Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) oversight, ULA said.

Retail Sees Long-Term Opportunity

Retail sentiment surrounding ASTS on Stocktwits remained ‘neutral’ over the past 24 hours, amid a 78% jump in message volumes.

One user believes ASTS is “going to be a great opportunity for long-term investors.”

View this Stocktwits post

ASTS shares have been under heavy selling pressure this year, tanking more than 61%.

data.title: Strong dollar, tighter Fed policy bets leave gold to languish at 14-month low
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bullion touched its lowest level since Sept 2025 in the session
  • Markets see 91% chance of a 25-bp rate hike next month
  • Recent computer outages, AI worries could lead investors to 'hard assets' like gold, analyst says

By Anjana Anil

Gold eased to a 14-month low on Thursday, as it continued to face pressure from strength in the US dollar, with markets fully pricing in a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting owing to stubborn inflation.

Spot gold was down 0.3% at $3,710.29 per ounce by 9:15 a.m. ET (1415 GMT), after touching its lowest level since September 2025 at $3,693.13 earlier in the session.

US gold futures for December delivery fell 0.8% to $3,711.50 per ounce.

"Interest rate expectations and a strong dollar are two factors weighing on gold prices today. Minutes from last month's FOMC meeting showed almost all Fed officials expected interest rates will need to move higher, and inflation data released since that meeting support further rate increases here in the US," said Chris Gaffney, head of World Markets at EverBank.

The dollar index this week reached its highest level since April 2, 2025, making greenback-priced commodities like gold more expensive for buyers holding other currencies.

Fed minutes released on Wednesday showed policymakers in October saw rising inflation risks that may warrant a stronger policy response.

The minutes reinforced sentiments already expressed by several policymakers throughout the week, including Governor Christopher Waller, who said the central bank may need to respond more aggressively to rising prices.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said he would likely support tighter monetary policy in an economy still facing inflation pressures.

Traders see a 91% chance of a 25-basis-point rate increase in December and a nearly 9% probability of a larger 50-basis-point hike, <FedWatch>.

Higher interest rates reduce the appeal of non-yielding bullion by raising its opportunity cost.

In the near-term, markets would need to see increased demand for gold from both consumers and central banks for prices to recover from the one-year low, Gaffney said, adding, "the recent computer outages, and worries about AI could lead investors to turn back toward 'hard assets' such as gold."

Spot silver rose 0.6% to $45.28 per ounce, platinum gained 0.7% to $1,380.30, and palladium fell 1.4% to $934.86.

data.title: SentinelOne and Singapore Digital and Intelligence Service Team Up to Strengthen Cyber Defence and Advance Secure AI
data.description:
SentinelOne® (), the AI Security leader, today announced it will partner with the Defence Cyber Command (DCCOM) of the Digital and Intelligence (DIS) to collaboratively strengthen cyber defence and advance secure AI across Singapore’s defence and critical infrastructure sectors. The relationship was formalised at CIDEX 2026.

The rapid adoption of AI has fundamentally changed cybersecurity norms and best practices. In the few months alone, the emergence and exploitation of novel vulnerabilities, rogue AI agent behavior, and LLM-related supply chain attacks, have ushered in a new era in cyber governance and defence.

SentinelOne and DCCOM will explore bringing together the AI-native Singularity™ Platform, SentinelLABS™ AI and threat intelligence research, and training with DCCOM’s own expertise to help defenders evolve their practices and strategies to meet this new reality. As a result, human defenders can benefit from AI-powered security to detect, investigate, and respond to novel threats at machine speed.

Security That Fits Defence Environments

Defence networks need protection that does not depend on a cloud connection. The Singularity Platform supports on-premise and air-gapped deployment, so DCCOM can apply AI-native protection in environments where a cloud connection is not an option. For defenders, that means detection and response that stay inside the network boundary.

Four Areas of Cooperation

The parties will explore partnering in four areas:

- Cybersecurity technology and solutions

- Cyber threat intelligence sharing

- Research and innovation

- Training and capacity building

“Singapore is putting AI at the centre of how it defends itself and runs its critical systems, and the security behind that has to keep pace,” said Andrew Howell, VP, Government Affairs at SentinelOne. “This collaboration allows us to explore ways our platform, our research, and our training can be combined alongside DCCOM's own teams, so defenders can stop attacks at machine speed, including in air-gapped environments, and so more of the people doing that work are trained in Singapore.”

“Our MOU with SentinelOne will facilitate joint collaboration on AI-enabled technologies for cyber operations, for faster threat detection, investigation and response at machine speed,” said Brigadier-General Clarence Cai, Commander DCCOM/Defence Cyber Chief.

About SentinelOne

SentinelOne () is the leader in AI security, setting the standard for using AI and automation to give defenders a decisive operating advantage. Built for those who secure our world, its platform delivers unified coverage across endpoints, identity, cloud, and AI. Powered by Autonomous Security Intelligence, SentinelOne stops attacks at machine speed, reducing risk and delivering clarity and control to stay one step ahead. Headquartered in Mountain View, California, with teams worldwide, SentinelOne protects nearly one-fifth of the Fortune 500 and hundreds of Global 2000 enterprises. From Main Street to Wall Street, the world's most critical organizations trust SentinelOne with their security.

data.title: Bath & Body Works Dips on Q3 Results
data.description:
Bath & Body Works, Inc. today reported third-quarter 2026 results.

The company reported net sales of $1,577 million for the quarter ended October 31, 2026, a decrease of 1.0% compared to net sales of $1,594 million for the quarter ended November 1, 2025.

Earnings per diluted share were $0.19 for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $0.37 last year. Third-quarter operating income was $108 million compared to $161 million last year, and net income was $38 million compared to $77 million last year.

CEO Daniel Heaf commented, “Our third-quarter results exceeded our sales and adjusted earnings per share guidance, and marks encouraging progress in our Consumer First Formula. One year after introducing this strategy, we are seeing our actions translate into results across product, brand, and marketplace.”

“Our product innovation is resonating with customers and digital delivered its second consecutive quarter of growth. Our wholesale business with Ulta and Amazon continues to gain momentum and we are telling bigger and bolder brand stories through a more coordinated approach to marketing. While these are encouraging early proof points, we have more work to do to drive consistent growth across our channels.”

BBWI shares lost 10 cents to $18.56.

data.title: Why Micron, Intel and other AI stocks are getting a lift on Thursday
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

Anthropic's IPO is one big reason - but there's also optimism about Texas's data-center landscape and a new buyback program from optical company Coherent

Micron's stock was up 6% on Thursday morning.

The Anthropic initial public offering is just one factor giving artificial-intelligence stocks a much-awaited boost on Thursday.

Shares of Coherent (COHR) were up 10% in morning trading. Shares of Lumentum Holdings (LITE), Micron Technology (MU), Marvell Technology (MRVL), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Nvidia (NVDA) were up between 4% and 6%.

Anthropic's IPO is "pivotal" for the AI investment cycle, D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria told MarketWatch. Shares start trading later today, and the company on Wednesday disclosed that it upsized the deal and priced it above its target range.

The company is a direct and indirect customer for chip makers, and the IPO has already been seen by investors as a bellwether for the AI trade.

Luria said that a successful IPO could "extend the cycle by years," while an unsuccessful one could "stall investment" into the ecosystem.

That said, it remains to be seen whether the Anthropic excitement can drive a more sustained rally for AI stocks, which have been pressured recently amid concerns about financing and Nvidia's leadership shakeup.

Morningstar analyst Martin Szumski doubts the IPO will "fully turn around what has been very bearish sentiment lately." One reason is that investors saw Anthropic's prospectus weeks ago and "know relatively what to expect."

He believes most of the "uplift" in the AI world on Thursday relates to Anthropic excitement, but he also noted Wednesday's announcement that Texas has resumed issuing permits for data centers after pausing them last month.

Texas is a key state in the data-center buildout, though there is still "some question whether this willingness to approve new proposals that are not currently under construction will continue," he said.

There are some other company-specific drivers of stock excitement on Thursday, including Coherent's announcement of a new buyback program, a CoreWeave executive's disclosure that he had purchased some company bonds and reports of Intel's remarks from a conference indicating that the company locked in an outside customer for its 18A manufacturing technology.

CoreWeave's stock (CRWV) stock is up 7% in morning trading, while Intel shares (INTC) are up 7%.

-Hannah Pedone
